decisiveReviewFindings: Historical signer prevented corrected-controller recovery; split controller and product source.
Source PATCH can be rejected after human review; attach source at new-version creation.
Upload UUID is deployed32hex; repaired initial36-only adapter fixture/validation.
Malformed JSON exceptions could quote provider bodies; fixed safe errors.
Client timeout can leave provider write in flight; source intent precedes both tag and AMO operations. Rejected a tag-only guard whose own mutation was ambiguous.
Newest20 candidates and first100 workflow runs could strand or endlessly retry work; full bounded/adaptive scans and retained bot-history reconciliation.
Published release could hide failed verification; inspect mandatory job step and retain bounded recovery/attention.
Current PR REST detail removed merge_commit_sha; read the merged issue event and verify locally against real PR3.
Permanently rejected builds/uploads need explicit retirement of unsubmitted intent; retain immutable intent and require reviewed evidence that no provider request remains in flight.

First new source-on-create AMO submission with inherited terms and readable source; delayed review and automatic resumption.
Approved Stackma signed permanent installation, complete immutable GitHub release/native attestations and repeat completion.
Historical tag and missing-tag merged-PR recovery under actual job token scopes, including workflow-write permission behavior.

assumptionsAndLimits: Earlier owner decisions are preserved as recorded in project docs; original conversation transcript not available.
Protected reviewed main, immutable source intent, one coordinated publishing authority; no conditional cross-provider transaction or protection against an outside administrator racing writes.
Latest-created AMO license inheritance/list ordering and shared object semantics depend on inspected deployed source; ambiguous predecessor timestamps/provider changes require investigation.
Pending metadata, sources and signed file can change; conflicts fail without overwrite.
Recovery depends on protected source and locked tool availability; reconstructed audit bytes that conflict with an existing draft require original-run/toolchain recovery.
Schedules can be delayed/dropped/disabled; run-history monitoring/counts cover retained evidence only.
All scan/resource bounds fail or report attention explicitly; they do not prove absence beyond the bound.
Hosted acceptance and literal optimality remain unestablished.

Retirement is an explicit operator assertion backed by actual outcome evidence, not machine proof of cancellation; unknown in-flight writes cannot be retired safely. Old controller runs must not restart after retirement.
